answer.evidence: This is a flat, face-on vegetable shelf. The top rows 1-4 are a light cornice strip, and row 5 is a darker line, but there is no eave shadow below it. Rows 6-8 are a light green valance drawn as a vertical strip, which reads as a face, not a sloped awning plane. Below that, the shelf interior (rows 9-26) is a vertical face with horizontal divider strips at rows 15-16, 21-22 and 27-29. The dividers show no top surface, so no horizontal plane is visible from above. The vegetables are decor. Overall this is a front elevation with at most a 1-2 row rim at the top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 19 visible tones per 16x16 tile, level with the stall-cheese (17) and well-roofed (20) references and well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0% and none of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted and not a black sticker line. By eye, the pale frame and shelf edges are separated by value and a dark tinted edge. Each produce row (greens, reds, yellows) is drawn as small clumps with highlight and shadow dots, and the backing panel is varied rather than flat. Shading is about 5 steps on the frame and produce against about 6 on the references. It is slightly simpler than the stall and well, but not thinner or flatter than the same-kind references. A careful artist would accept it beside them.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a veg-display wall with a white/grey frame and shelves holding green, red and yellow produce. surfaces.part: top frame / header band with green stripe

answer.evidence: This is a flat, face-on display unit. A light frame runs around the edge: rows 1-4 at the top, thin rim strips down both sides, and rows 28-29 at the bottom. The top band (rows 1-4) is the same frame rim as the other sides, just thicker, and it merges straight into a green header stripe (rows 5-8) that reads as a front-facing sign. The only dark line, at row 5, divides two vertical strips. No eave shadow or foreshortened horizontal plane follows it. Below, the shelf ledges at rows 15-16 and 21-22 are 1-2 row light strips with yellow tags, and they read as front faces. The shelves are a back wall of produce seen straight on (dark backing at rows 9-14, 17-20 and 23-26). No ellipse, no roof plane and no contents seen from above appear anywhere. So there is no real top surface, only a rim of about 2 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a grey-white shelf of vegetables with a pale frame and rows of red, green and yellow produce. Measured facts are close to the references: 19 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted and not a black sticker line. By eye, the frame and glass panel use only about 3-4 steps (white, light grey, mid grey, dark grey-green), which is thinner than the 5-6 steps on Beodeul wood and roof materials. The produce is made of small clusters, but each has little individual shading, so the piece reads somewhat flatter and more graphic than the stall or well. Density is close to the references on the numbers but slightly lower in craft. It is acceptable in kind, yet a careful artist would likely see it as a little thin next to the stall, so the call is a fail given the instruction to fail when in doubt.
